The nose is packed with black fruit, especially blackberries and plums, with slight spicy overtones hinting at black pepper and cinnamon. Sweet, soft tannins come together in a closely-woven texture that merges with the fruit, while a crisp fresheness provides a long, tasty finish.

name: Fontanafredda  Langhe Rosso Eremo DOC
wine_color: Ruby red colour with garnet reflexes.
desc_en_short: Ruby red colour with garnet reflexes. The bouquet is reminiscent of underbrush (red currant, blackberry, blueberry), prune jam, licorice, with nuances of chocolate and toasted coffee. On the palate the sweet and smooth tannins of Nebbiolo give volume, roundness and mingle with the acidity of Barbera, giving freshness and sapidity to the aftertaste.

name: Fontanafredda  Barbera D'Alba Raimonda DOC
wine_color: The colour is deep ruby-red when young, it tends to garnet-red on ageing.
desc_en_short: The colour is deep ruby-red when young, it tends to garnet-red on ageing. It has a rather intense, characteristic nose which is flowery and fruity at the same time, with nice light overtones of wood, spices and vanilla. The flavour is full, persistent, nicely dry and velvety. The wine is already perfect to drink one years after the vintage. Its character and personality will becompleted by a further period of ageing in the bottle.

name: Fontanafredda  Barolo DOCG
desc_en_short:
Deep garnet red colour. Distinct floral and red fruit notes on the nose, ending with sensations reminiscent of
pine resin, camphor and apricot jam. The palate is fresh, rich, with notes of liquorice and pink pepper.

name: Fontanafredda  Vigna La Rosa Barolo DOCG
wine_color: Garnet colour with intense ruby reflexes.
desc_en_short: The single-vineyard Barolos are produced from the most painstaking selections carried out in vineyards which tradition has preserved over time as emblems of exemplary quality. “La Rosa” represents an interpretation of Barolo of particular importance: even though it is the soil and the sun – or what is called in short microclimate – which commands man and guides his technical decisions, and not vice versa. Garnet colour with intense ruby reflexes. The bouquet shows hints of very mature fruits and spices. In the mouth very ripe tannins give a sweet and persistent taste. “La Rosa” expresses the qualities of the Barolos grown in Serralunga d’Alba at their best, with a marked – almost feminine – concession to grace and softness in its flavour and bouquet.

name: Casarena Reservado Cabernet Sauvignon
wine_color: It is an elegant and complex wine, with a deep red ruby color.
desc_en_short: Grapes go through a double manual cluster and berry selection. After a careful destemming, the berries go through a cold whole-berry fermentation. To assure its maximum aromatic expression, a natural alcoholic fermentation is triggered first, at low temperatures. In oak barrels, the wine experiments a spontaneous malolactic fermentation and then it is naturally clarified.

name: Casarena Single Vineyard Naoki Malbec
wine_color: Deep red purplish color, bright with violet hues.
desc_en_short: Grapes go through a double hand selection of clusters and berries. After a careful destemming, the fruit performs a cold maceration with whole berries. To assure a maximum aromatic expression, we start with a natural alcoholic fermentation at low temperatures. In oak barrels, the wine experiments a spontaneous malolactic fermentation and it is naturally clarified.

name: Di Majo Norante Ramitello Biferno Rosso DOC
wine_color: Deep ruby red in colour with violet reflections.
desc_en_short: Full, mellow and velvety wine; with a perfect blend of flavours such as plum, undergrowth and hints of leather and licorice, deep ruby red in colour with violet reflections.

name: Di Majo Norante Tintilia del Molise DOC
wine_color: Deep ruby red color with purple hues.
desc_en_short: Tintilia is a black-skinned grape indigenous to the small region of Molise. It is grown in very small quantities. Tintilia wines tend to a rich, ruby red in color and are full-bodied, with evident, yet soft, tannins.

name: Di Majo Norante Don Luigi Riserva Molise DOC
wine_color: Opaque ruby in color with garnet reflections.
desc_en_short: Red wine Don Luigi is the flagship product of our winery. It is a wine made from carefully selected best and the most mature grapes of Montepulciano.

name: Pajaru Meridionale Tre Tenute - Organic
desc_en_short: Aromas and flavors of cherry-based confiture with hints of balsamic and cigar box. Full-bodied with the same savory tones dominating the palate. The tannins are fine and are sinking into the wine. Long, tasty finish

name: Chateau de la Maltroye  Bourgogne Pinot Noir
desc_en_short: This is such an attractive wine representing all that we like about Burgundy: ripe juicy fruit, good fresh tannins, a lively acidity and a round, lasting taste. The wine comes from the lower slopes of Jean-Pierre Cournut’s vineyards in Chassagne-Montrachet. This good pedigree shows in the spicy, fruity taste and the full, satisfying body.

name: Chateau de la Maltroye  Santenay 1er Cru "La Comme" Rouge
desc_en_short: From Château de la Maltroye, this Premier Cru Santenay 'La Comme' is a soulful Pinot Noir bursting with damson plum, Moroccan spice, and cedar, delivering a silky, polished palate that showcases the earthy elegance Santenay's finest vineyards are known for.

name: Chateau de la Maltroye  Chassagne-Montrachet 1er Cru “Clos du Chateau de La Maltroye” - Monopole - Rouge
desc_en_short: ณt is very aromatic with fresh, pure flavours of soft berried fruit and cherries. It has such silkiness and sweetness that it is easy to overlook the depth here. Vibrant with aromas of sloes and violets underlain with spicy notes, this is a wine which will take two years of so to be ready to drink but will be very rewarding. It is delicious.

name: Chateau de la Maltroye  Chassagne-Montrachet 1er Cru "Clos Saint Jean" - Rouge
desc_en_short: The suave, round and delicious medium-bodied flavors possess a seductive mid-palate texture, all wrapped in a less mineral-driven but more complex finale that is slightly firmer. This offers very good development potential yet could also be approached young if desired.

name: Albert Bichot  Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru "Petite Chapelle"
desc_en_short: Deep nose with aromas reminiscent of ripe red and black fruit (strawberry, raspberry...) and mild spices mingle with a delicate hint of oak. This well-balanced wine is rich and fleshy, and boasts a finely structured palate for an elegant overall impression. Long and very fragrant on the finish.

name: Albert Bichot  Morey-Saint-Denis 1er Cru "les Sorbets"
desc_en_short: The intense nose is redolent of red and black fruit (raspberry, blackcurrant, raspberry...) combined with a delicate touch of oak, which will evolve over time towards more complex scents (spices, forest undergrowth, leather...). Fleshy and full bodied on the palate, this wine offers pleasing structure that lends it perfect balance. The long finish is silky and deliciously fruity.

name: Albert Bichot  Chambolle-Musigny 1er Cru "les Chabiots"
desc_en_short: From a storied Premier Cru climat adjacent to Les Amoureuses in Chambolle-Musigny, this Albert Bichot Pinot Noir seduces with delicate red fruit, rose-petal florals, and silky tannins, finishing with an elegant whisper of menthol and tobacco.

name: Chateau De Camparian Pessac Leognan
wine_color: The wine is deep and bright in colour.
desc_en_short:
Château de Camparian has been owned by the Ballande family for over 150 years and is one of the last vineyards in the commune of Villenave d'Ornon.

The property is situated in the gateway of Bordeaux in the appelation of Pessac-Léognan and the wine is produced by traditional vinifaction methods and aged in oak for 12 months.

name: Château Citran  Cru Bourgeois Haut Medoc
desc_en_short:
Château Citran is one of the oldest estates in the Médoc. The Donissan de Citran family reigned over
this former Médoc seigneury from the 13th century until 1832.
 n 1996, the Merlaut family, already deeply involved in the Bordeaux wine industry, took over
the beautiful estate. Today, Citran has over 80 hectares of vines in the Haut-Médoc appellation. These
are planted with premium grape varieties that make the most of its fine terroir: Cabernet Sauvignon,
Merlot, and Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot.
A healthy balance between traditional and modern techniques prevails in both the vineyard and
cellars to produce a very elegant and distinguished wine.

name: La Demoiselle de Sociando Mallet Second wine of Château Sociando Mallet
desc_en_short: The Second Wine of one of the most famous estates in the Médoc appellation, an introduction to the Sociando-Mallet style. La Demoiselle de Sociando-Mallet offers a fresh and fruity wine, easy and pleasant to drink from a young age.

name: L”Orme De Rauzan Gassies Haut Medoc
Bernard Magrez l'Ame de Pape Clement
desc_en_short: L'Ame de Pape Clément Rouge is a full-bodied, complex wine with a deep ruby color and aromas of ripe blackberry, cassis, and dark cherry. On the palate, it has a velvety texture with flavors of blackberry, plum, and dark chocolate. The tannins are well-integrated and the finish is long and lingering.

name: Calice De Faugeres Saint Emilion Grand Cru Second wine of Chateau Faugeres
Chateau d'Aiguilhe Castillon Cotes De Bordeaux
desc_en_short: "A major sleeper of the vintage, this wine is from Stephan von Neipperg. This gorgeous wine, which is Merlot-dominated with some Cabernet Franc, has turned out to be excellent and is certainly one of the real value picks in 2013. Most people would be smart to taste it out of bottle, but it is loaded. Dense ruby/purple with notes of cedar wood, Christmas fruitcake, spice box and creme de cassis, it has a surprisingly good and lush texture, light tannins and adequate acidity. Drink it over the next 7-8 years."

name: Relais De La Dominique Saint Emilion Grand Cru Second wine of Chateau La Dominique
desc_en_short:
Ideally located in the north-west of the Saint-Emilion appellation, Château La Dominique is a vineyard since the 16th century. Close to the Châteaux Cheval Blanc, Figeac, l'Evangile and La Conseillante, the vineyard has been owned by the Fayat family since 1969.

Today, the estate judiciously combines authenticity and modernity with its contemporary cellar designed by the architect Jean Nouvel. Relais de la Dominique is the second wine of the property.

name: Les Hauts de Lynch-Moussas Second wine of Chateau Lynch-Moussas
desc_en_short:
Les Hauts de Lynch-Moussas, second wine of
Château Lynch-Moussas, classified as a Grand Cru
Classé in 1855, was created in 2001 by Philippe
Castéja succeeding to his father, Emile. The name
comes from the name of the vineyards situated
just above the estate. On the sorting table,
essentially the grapes from the youngest vines
are used to make the wine which is however
elaborated with the same care and same high
standards as for the « Premier Vin ».

name: Les Fiefs De Lagrange Saint-Julien Second wine of Chateau Lagrange
desc_en_short: Created in 1983 in order to increase the quality of the Grand Vin through a more drastic selection, the second wine of Château Lagrange was among the first in this category and is today appraised for its intrinsic qualities. Vinified from vines that are already 30 years old on average, half of which are Cabernet Sauvignon, and aged for thirteen months in barrels which are 20% new, it is characterized by supple tannins and offers substantial ageing potential. With a very pure elegance from the beginning, it will gain in depth and intensity over the years.

name: Chateau Pibran Pauillac
desc_en_short: Château Pibran opens with a subtle bouquet with notes of black fruits, crème de cassis, plum, blueberry, white flowers, cedar wood, toasted oak and graphite. On the palate, it is an opulent and structured Pauillac, with juicy substance and silky, crunchy tannins. Frank, fresh and with a nice balance between fruitiness and acidity, it sails slowly towards its peak.

name: Château Montviel  Pomerol
desc_en_short: The 2016 Montviel is medium to deep garnet-purple colored with tobacco, redcurrants, menthol and black soil with blackberries and blueberries plus a waft of fallen leaves. The palate is medium-bodied, chewy, lively and earthy, finishing just a bit lean.

name: Les Tourelles de Longueville Pauillac
wine_color: Deep ruby red, reflecting vibrant fruit and youthful energy.
style: Merlot 55%, Cabernet Sauvignon 27%, Cabernet Franc 13%, Petit Verdot 5%
desc_en_short: Les Tourelles de Longueville is the elegant second label of Château Pichon Baron, delivering classic Pauillac depth with a Merlot-forward softness — silky, generous, and unmistakably Left Bank in character.

name: Casal Bordino Collezione Bordino Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC
style: Montepulciano (มอนเตพูลเชียโน)
desc_en_short: Smooth and rich Montepulciano with dark fruit, spices, and chocolate hints — perfect for grilled meats, tomato-based pasta, and cheeses.

name: Betto Meremma Toscana
desc_en_short: Rich and smooth Tuscan red blending ripe dark fruits, herbs, and soft spices — perfect for grilled meats, pasta, and hearty Mediterranean dishes.

name: Domaine Pierre-André Dumas Alchimie Cote de Brouilly
desc_en_short: A sophisticated Gamay from Côte de Brouilly — elegant floral, red fruit, and spice notes with silky tannins. Perfect with red meats and game.

name: Chateau Lynch Bages  AOC Pauillac 2020
wine_color: Deep purple-black, reflecting intensity and youthful vibrancy.
desc_en_short:
Château Lynch-Bages 2020 is driven by the intensity of Cabernet Sauvignon and softened by the richness of Merlot. The structure is firm with refined tannins, and the flavor profile reveals layer after layer of depth and elegance.

This wine embodies a “classic yet modern” style—it feels solid and composed, yet vibrant. Ideal for those who love powerful Bordeaux reds that are approachable in youth but also capable of aging gracefully for decades.

name: Marchile Cabernet Sauvignon
style: Cabernet Sauvignon (คาเบอร์เนต์ โซวีญง)
desc_en_short: A bold Cabernet Sauvignon from Maule Valley, Chile—vibrant red fruit, plum, cherry, and cocoa with firm tannins and refreshing acidity. A well-structured wine for grilled meats and rich dishes.

name: Chateau Haut-Brion  1er Grand Cru Classe 2020
wine_color: The color is a beautiful purplish red.
desc_en_short:
Château Haut-Brion is a First Growth in the Bordeaux Wine Official Classification of 1855. It is located in Pessac, Graves just one mile (2 km) from the city of Bordeaux. The vineyard consists of 109 acres (441,000 m²) producing 12,000 to 15,000 cases of wine each year. Located in the Graves region, it was the only non-Médoc estate to be included in the 1855 classification.

The cultivation of the vineyard of the château Haut-Brion in the middle of town with jealous care, its ability to age more than its neighbours – up to about twenty years, or even more, the men working under the lead of Jean Delmas, the modern cuvier, the artisitcally lead winemaking…. All this contributes to the success of a domainn, producing the greatest red wines and rare white wines.
Average age of vines is 30 years.

Château Bahans Haut-Brion, although a second wine, has the same treatment throughout as Château Haut-Brion. Grown on the same land as Château Haut-Brion, Château Bahans Haut-Brion, profits from the same planting and harvest techniques, and has the advantage of the same rigorous selection and thoroughness in vinification as the "Grand Vin".

name: Chateau La Mission Haut-Brion  Grand Cru Classe 2017
brand: Chateau La Mission Haut-Brion  Grand Cru Classe
desc_en_short: A blend of 56% Merlot, 40% Cabernet Sauvignon and 4% Cabernet Franc, the first impression is of balance and restraint. Lovely briar and sloe flavours in the nose, mineral, graphite aromas that lead to a long and fruity nose woven with earthy and smoky notes. As good as the impressive 2001, this wine will always lie in the shadow of the 2015 and 2016 which is a pity because this is a great wine.

name: Chateau Le Marquis De Calon Segur  "Le 2nd Vin De Chateau Calon Segur" 2014
desc_en_short: "The estate’s Second Wine offers a different interpretation of the Calon terroir. With an average of 75% Merlot in the blends, Le Marquis de Calon Ségur is totally distinct from the First Wine. “It benefits from a true expression of its own”, underlines Vincent Millet. “The plots are separated out from the beginning.” Le Marquis de Calon Ségur provides immediate enjoyment, warmth and a velvety texture. It is carefully aged generally for 17 months in oak barrels, a third of which are new. Deliciously easy-drinking, silky and expressive, its charm comes to the fore, while at the same time bringing to our minds the elegance of the Grand Vin."

name: Chateau Calon Segur  3eme Cru Classe 2017
desc_en_short: Medium to deep garnet-purple colored, the 2017 Calon-Ségur features warm plums, cassis, baked cherries and mulberries, earth, meats and cedar on the nose with notes of lavender and olives. The palate is medium-bodied, elegant and intense with firm, fine-grained tannins and great length, finishing minerally. This wine was aged in 100% new French oak barrels for 20 months.

name: Chateau Haut Bages  Monpelou Cru Bourgeois Superieur 2016
desc_en_short: This château’s vines are superbly situated on the plateau of one of Pauillac’s best sectors. It rubs shoulders with vineyards belonging to classed growths Grand-Puy-Ducasse and Lynch-Moussas, and until 1948 formed part of the 4th Growth Ch Duhart-Milon. The 2016 has been assembled from 68% Cabernet Sauvignon, 27% Merlot and 5% Cabernet Franc, and aged in 60% new barrels. Colour is medium-deep ruby, with fine, open aromas which leap from the glass. Palate has imposing, full-bodied structure, with concentrated fruitiness, freshness and length. A superb wine ready for immediate enjoyment.

name: Almaviva  2021
wine_color: Its color is garnet with a purple sheen.
style: Cabernet Sauvignon, 22% Carmenère (From Peumo), 5% Cabernet Franc, 2% Petit Verdot
grape_variety: Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, Merlot
desc_en_short:
The 2021 Almaviva is a blend primarily based on Cabernet Sauvignon and Carmenere, but not limited to these, and was aged for up to 18 months in French barrels. Its color is garnet with a purple sheen. The enticing nose showcases blackberry, cassis marmalade, black and green pepper, ashes, camphor and cigar box aromas. Indulgent and rich on the palate, it carries taut, fine-grained tannins, velvet texture and balanced acidity, leading to a long, ripe finish. This bold and layered red wine reveals nuanced depth and richness on the palate, promising further development as it matures in the bottle. - Joaquín Hidalgo, Vinous Media

Awards.

98 Point by James Suckling

96 Point by Robert Parker's Wine Advocate

name: Domaine Thibault Liger-Belair  Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru ""les Saint Georges""
desc_en_short: This is an epic wine in the cellar of Thibault Liger-Belair, tannic, powerful and deep. The fruit character is dark plum and blackberry with hints of smoke, leather, and cigar leaf. The texture is dense and tannic; the finish is long. Every aspect of this is substantial, yet it retains the elegance to appear perhaps even more sophisticated than the Clos Vougeot. In my opinion, it is certainly on the level of the grand cru wines

name: Graca 28  Reserva Douro DOC
style: Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz, Tinta Barroca, Tinto Cão
desc_en_short: The wine, made from the noblest Douro grapes, shows elegance and balanced with a fantastic aromatic intensity of wild fruits, and refined spice notes in a long and velvety end of mouth.

name: Chateau Grand Soreillon  Bordeaux Superior
desc_en_short: Château Grand Sorillon Bordeaux Supérieur A joyous Bordeaux Supérieur – our favourite find of recent years. Juicy and fruit forward, with red fruit prominence and light tannins. The wine is approachable, open and fruity and is ready to drink.

name: Antinori  Solaia IGT 2020
food_matching: Pasta, Pizza, Roasted Chicken, Pork, Medium Cheese

name: Masseto  Toscana IGT 2020
desc_en_short: Masseto 2020 is one of Italy's most iconic single-vineyard Merlots, delivering extraordinary concentration, balsamic depth, and the hallmark structured tannins that define this legendary Bolgheri estate — a wine built unmistakably for the long haul.

name: Masseto  Toscana IGT 2021
desc_en_short: A harmony of vibrant, mysterious aromas welcomes the nose into every glass of Masseto 2021. These aromas continue on the palate. The wine elegantly and captivatingly fills the mouth with succulence, juice and persistence. Masseto 2021 is a wine that knows how to impress, persisting throughout the tasting, with its savory aftertaste and fullness of expression. The appreciative manifesto of the rich 2021 vintage.

name: Masseto  Toscana IGT 2012
desc_en_short: The 2012 vintage combines the principal characteristics of a great Masseto: rich and generous but also very fresh and with a firm structure in a wine of great intensity and complexity. The color is intense and dark, olfactory impact develops classic notes of red and black fruit, chocolate and liquorice, subtly enhanced by the toasting of the wood. The palate shows well-rounded and full, with a thick, dense tannic texture that boasts rich fruit and spice notes. The finish is prolonged with a lively and vibrant acid vein that closes on a note of intense freshness.

name: Concha Y Toro  The Master Cabernet Sauvignon
desc_en_short: Deep, dark red. Black fruit aromas like cherries, cassis and blackberries, along with notes of cedar and a smoky hint. The mouth is velvety, framing a firm tannic structure and the finish is very long with pronounced flavours.

name: Riporta  Primitivo Puglia
desc_en_short: Medium Ruby in the glass with notes of dusty gravel, red clay, nuts, coffee beans, and an iron minerality. Dry and full bodied with low tannins and acidity, the palate is juicy with mixed berries, baking spices, earth, leather, and oak leading to a pleasant finish. Easy sipper!

name: Concha Y Toro  Terrunyo Cabernet Sauvignon
desc_en_short: Concha y Toro's Terrunyo Cabernet Sauvignon is a single-vineyard expression from Chile's premium terroir, delivering vivid red fruit, graphite, and tea-leaf complexity with elegantly velvety tannins and a fresh, vibrant palate.

name: Riporta  Sangiovese
desc_en_short: Garnet red in colour this wine has seen 20% aged in oak. A medium bodied wine which is balanced and ready to drink. Excellent pairing with any Italian dishes, both lighter and heavier in style.

name: Tornatore  Etna Rosso Trimarchisa
wine_color: Ruby red with faint violet hues.
desc_en_short: Ruby red with faint violet hues. Rich and complex on the nose, very reminiscent of small brambly fruits, black cherry and a very delicate hint of sweet wood. The palate is firm, complex and extraordinarily persistent.

name: Tornatore  Etna Rosso Riserva
desc_en_short: Intense ruby red, typical mineral notes on the nose, with clear hints of red fruits, especially morello cherry, caper, seaweed and red mulberries. In the mouth it is crisp, fresh with surprising savory length and fullness. Endowed with good structure denoting sure longevity. Alcohol content 14%.

name: Chateau Margaux  2021
desc_en_short: 96 points in James Suckling The purity of fruit here is terrific, with redcurrants, blackcurrants, licorice, lead pencil and hints of fresh basil—so aromatic—that follow through to a full body with creamy, round tannins and lots of volume and fluidity in the center-palate for the vintage. Very structured at the end. 87% cabernet sauvignon, 8% merlot, 3% cabernet franc and 2% petit verdot. Leave this for at least five or six years. Try after 2030.

name: Chateau Margaux  2020
desc_en_short:
100 points in James Suckling

Gorgeous aromas of dark plums and violets. Orange peel, too. Some crushed stone. Bark. Stems. Iron shavings. Full-bodied, but very tight and compacted. The tannins are all here making it very structured, yet they are polished and melted together. Needs years to show all of its greatness. Incredible polish and structure. More structured than the 2019.

name: Chateau Margaux  2018
desc_en_short:
100 points in James Suckling

So much ash, tobacco and earth to the bright blackberry and currant aromas. Flowers too. Fresh. Full-bodied with seamless tannins that spread across your palate and caress every square centimeter. It’s shows loads of ripe-berry, cherry, currant and chocolate character, as well as walnut and light cedar. Then the finish goes on for minutes. Extremely refined and elegant, despite the structure. 90% cabernet sauvignon, 4% cabernet franc, 4% merlot and 2% petit verdot. A joy to taste, but drink after 2025.

name: Chateau Margaux  2010
desc_en_short:
100 points in James Suckling

This was phenomenal from barrel and remains so. The aromas are spellbinding. It smells like a bouquet of pink roses and then goes to currants, berries and citrus. Full body, with wonderfully refined tannins. It starts discretely and then grows to different levels and dimensions like a slow but big high tide. The texture is so beautiful. Try it in 2020 or beyond.

name: Chateau Margaux  2000
desc_en_short:
100 points in James Suckling

This is like smelling an amazing bouquet of flowers, deep and thought provoking. Notes of raspberries, and strawberries round out the refined nose. Full and silky. More than just silk really, it is almost transparent. Incredibly mellow, yet enticing. It is difficult to find the perfect word. It is as ethereal as Paul Pontieller, managing director of Chateaux Margaux says. The impeccable balance makes this perfect to drink now, but it will get even better with more time. This is already ageless.

name: E. Guigal  Cote Rotie La Mouline
wine_color: Ruby red with red vermillion tints.
desc_en_short: The Côte-Rôtie “La Mouline” is one of the most emblematic of the Guigal domain’s wines. Small quantities are produced each year from a vineyard in the heart of the 'côte blonde'. This is a voluptuous, silky and intensely aromatic wine.

name: E. Guigal  Cote Rotie La Turque
wine_color: Deep ruby red with dark tints.
desc_en_short: Côte-Rôtie "La Turque" is one of the flagship of the Domaine GUIGAL. A powerful wine with spicy notes, its terroirs from côte brune with “blond accents” lends it a great elegance.

name: Corryton Burge  Barossa Cabernet
desc_en_short: Aromas of blackcurrants and blackberry with subtle notes of eucalypt leaf and cedar. The palate is rich and elegant with blackcurrent, coffee and dark chocolate. The oak is well intergrated into the wine, and the tannins are firm but are nicely balanced in the finish.

name: Corryton Burge  The Brigadier Barossa Cabernet Sauvignon
desc_en_short: Aromas of blackcurrants and blackberry with subtle notes of eucalypt leaf and cedar. The palate is rich and elegant with blackcurrent, coffee and dark chocolate. The oak is well intergrated into the wine, and the tannins are firm but are nicely balanced in the finish. Enjoy now or if your willpower is strong this can be cellared for up to 10 years.

name: Corryton Burge  Percival Norman Barossa Shiraz
wine_color: Deep red with very vibrant purple hues.
desc_en_short:
Deep red with very vibrant purple hues. Multi-layered aroma of sweet raspberry coulis, chocolate truffles and toasty oak. A bold and rich palate featuring raspberry and chocolate, the fruit-forward palate is matched by its bold tannin structure.

Pair with dukkha-crusted lamb backstrap served with charred broccolini, roasted vine cherry tomatoes and a cumin-spiced yogurt and lemon dressing.

name: Siro Pacenti  Brunello Di Montalcino Vecchie Vigne DOCG 2017
desc_en_short: Siro Pacenti’s “Vecchie Vigne” (Old Vines) is the estate’s flagship Brunello, produced from the oldest Sangiovese vines planted before 1980. Giancarlo Pacenti blends tradition and innovation, crafting a wine that reflects both the rugged soul of Montalcino and the refinement of modern winemaking. This cuvée is a tribute to his family’s deep roots and a benchmark for Brunello excellence.

name: Siro Pacenti  Brunello Di Montalcino Vecchie Vigne DOCG 2018
wine_color: Deep ruby with garnet reflections, youthful yet refined
desc_en_short: Siro Pacenti's Vecchie Vigne Brunello di Montalcino 2018 draws from old vines planted in the early 1980s across Montalcino's northern and southern slopes, delivering a wine of remarkable structure, layered complexity, and the precise, purity-driven style that has made Giancarlo Pacenti one of the appellation's most celebrated producers.

name: Siro Pacenti Brunello Di Montalcino Vecchie Vigne DOCG (Value Set of 3) (Vintage 2016, 2017, 2018)
desc_en_short:
A Rare Vertical Set from Montalcino’s Master of Precision

Indulge in a rare vertical tasting experience featuring three remarkable vintages (2016, 2017, 2018) of Siro Pacenti’s iconic "Vecchie Vigne" Brunello—crafted exclusively from old-vine Sangiovese planted in the early 1980s.

This value set offers a collector-level journey into Montalcino terroir, vintage variation, and Giancarlo Pacenti’s masterful style—uniting power, purity, and aging potential in every bottle.

Highlights:

Single-Estate, Old Vine Fruit – From 35–45-year-old Sangiovese vines on both north & south slopes of Montalcino

Vertical Vintage Expression – Showcases vintage personalities side-by-side:

  • 2016 – Classic, structured, age-worthy (Landmark vintage – 100 pts JS)
  • 2017 – Bold, intense, and generous with concentration
  • 2018 – Cool-climate elegance, floral, and mineral-driven finesse

Aged in French oak barriques, integrating modern finesse with traditional soul

Perfect for collectors, gifting, or sommelier-led tastings

name: Castelli Shiraz Great Southern
wine_color: Deep crimson with a vibrant purple hue, indicating youthful intensity and structure.
desc_en_short: Crafted in the cool-climate vineyards of Great Southern, Western Australia, Castelli Shiraz is a refined expression of power and elegance. This bottle delivers bold character and silky balance, making it a modern classic of Australian Shiraz.

name: Famille Jaume  Domaine La Main Des Momes
desc_en_short:
Aromas of black fruits, with hints of licorice and spice. The 
palate is smooth and generous, balanced by a refreshing 
acidity and a pleasant velvety texture.

name: Doix
desc_en_short: Very fine, clean blend of raspberry and plum, light notes of potpourri, white pepper, dried orange peel, minor tobacco, and a bit of sweet licorice. Very fresh and juicy on the palate, fine fruit with even finer tannins, lifted acidity that carries the wine along e ortlessly.

name: Talenti Brunello di Montalcino Riserva Pian di Conte (Magnum) (1.5 L)
wine_color: Ruby red and intense colour  with orange shimmers.
desc_en_short: A top-tier, structured, and age-worthy Brunello Riserva, representing the pinnacle of the Talenti estate.

name: Chateau Lafite-Rothschild  2020
wine_color: Very dark color, with purple glints, indicating that the wine is still very much in its youth.
desc_en_short: 100 points James Suckling - "Amazing aromas here with tobacco, crushed stone, cigar box, currants, tar, and lead pencil, as well as spices, iron, and dried ginger. Medium- to full-bodied, with a density and tightness. Very compact and complex. Racy. Delicacy with strength. Orange peel undertones. A wine to contemplate. You must understand it to understand the great Lafites of the past and those of the future. Only 12.8% alcohol. 92% cabernet sauvignon, 7% merlot and 1% petit verdot. Best after 2030, but drink it if you have the chance taste it."

name: Tenuta dell'Ornellaia  Ornellaia Bolgheri DOC "La Proportione" (Artist Label) 2020
wine_color: he intense and dark colour heralds a wine of beautiful
desc_en_short: Artist Joseph Kosuth was invited to interpret the character of the 2020 vintage for the Vendemmia d’Artista project. In addition to creating a site-specific work, he styled a series of large-format bottles with his art. Furthermore, for the Bordeaux bottle, the artist designed a limited-edition label alongside the traditional label.

name: Feudi Bizantini  Terre Dei Rumi Montepulciano D’Abruzzo D.O.P.
wine_color: Ruby red color with purplish reflections.
desc_en_short:
Ruby red color with purplish
reflections. The nose shows layers
of plum and red cherry aromas,
with blueberry, blackcurrant, and
savory red fruits. Medium-bodied,
softly textured, and with great
fruit intensity

name: Chateau Lafleur Pomerol 2020 (Magnum) (1.5 L)
desc_en_short: 100 points James Suckling - "This red shows such beautiful and ripe aromas of blackberries, orange peel, hazelnuts, and tropical fruits. It's full-bodied, with superb texture of polished tannins that are velvety. The length last for minutes. It's muscular yet elegant. It flexes it muscle yet pulls them back. What gorgeous tone to this young red. Try in 2020."

name: Chateau Latour 2013
desc_en_short: Composed of 95.2% Cabernet Sauvignon, 4.4% Merlot and 0.4% Petit Verdot, the 2013 Latour offers an open-knit, fragrant nose of licorice, sandalwood, rose petals and cigar box over a core of Black Forest cake, stewed plums, mulberries and redcurrant jelly, plus a waft of cast-iron pan. The elegantly styled, medium-bodied palate (13% alcohol) fills the mouth with intense red and black berry preserves layers, framed by evolved, soft-textured tannins and well-knit freshness, finishing long and spicy. This vintage does not have the power and backbone of an outstanding vintage of Latour, but it is aging gracefully and, still possessing a lot of discernible fruit with plenty of tertiary pizazz, is absolutely delicious to drink right now. This sweet-spot stage is likely to continue for another 5-7 years, before the wine plateaus at a maturity peak and holds for a further 15+ years

name: Chateau Ducru Beaucaillou 2017
desc_en_short: Ducru is on top form these days. Bruno Borie has made some very serious wines at Ducru in recent vintages with many vats previously destined for the grand vin now being used for the second label. From 2003 onwards production of the first wine has been reduced from 15,000-20,000 cs to 9,000-11,000 cs. There is now more second wine - La Croix de Beaucaillou - than there is Grand Vin. Bruno's policy is now to only select fruit from the heart of the Ducru vineyard, overlooking the estuary for the Grand Vin. Ducru is clearly back where it belongs at the top of the super-second league.

name: Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret Grands-Echezeaux Grand Cru
desc_en_short:
Character of the wine

To the Eye : A pure bright deep red, truly stunning. Clear and limpid, the shifting colour nuances often vary, though generally tending towards fairly dark shades of garnet or violet-purple: a colour that holds the eye.

To the Nose : With age, the palette tends towards pepper and musk, animal pelts, leather and spices, prunes. Sometimes the bouquet hints at scents of woodland undergrowth, moss, mushrooms, damp earth, game, fruit preserved in alcohol and mulberries round off this range of aromas. Especially in young wines, one may well encounter scents of pine, dog roses, violets and fresh cherries.

In the Mouth : Peaceful and dreamy, serene with age, subtle and refined, this wine fully reveals the complex nature of a really good Burgundy, all the art that can be achieved through the medium of pinot noir grapes grown on one particular terroir. The structure is outstanding: solid, full-bodied, rich and exceptionally harmonious. It is wholly appropriate for the qualification Great to precede Echezeaux in the name Grands-Echezeaux: it has that extra touch of class, of vinosity, and a dense and subtle texture.

name: Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret Echezeaux Grand Cru
desc_en_short:
Character of the wine

Echezeaux wines are a clear garnet or ruby red, the exact hue often varying considerably. When young these wines have vanilla-scented, smoky, woody aromas or a hint of torrefaction, combined with suggestions of red fruits and spices. After a few years the nose becomes vegetable or animal, with scents of mushrooms, truffles or woodland undergrowth. The great complexity of the bouquet makes this a wine both rich and feminine; fat and mellow, with fine, delicate and fairly supple tannins. In the mouth the attack is spirited, the balance pleasant and there is a succulent fullness with aromas of red fruits.

name: Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret Echezeaux Grand Cru "la Grande Complication"
desc_en_short:
Character of the wine

Just like the precision and know-how of the best watchmakers, each bouquet from our Grande Complication is expressed with purity and authenticity.

First, the wild berries - intense blackcurrant and lively raspberry- reveal all of the splendour of this selection of grains. Then, the subtleness of the aromas comes out as sweet spicy notes. Then there’s silence.

Harmony, power, finesse and purity blend in a precious and complex movement. The scale of the site is perfectly calibrated and the grandeur of the Pinot Noir is sublimating. Our Grande Complication requires time to express itself with the emotions more intense as this exceptional quest goes on.

name: Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret Echezeaux Grand Cru "la Grande Complication" (Magnum) (1.5 L)

name: Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret Richebourg Grand Cru
desc_en_short: One of Burgundy's most revered Grand Crus, Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret's Richebourg delivers an intoxicating portrait of Vosne-Romanée — opulent yet precise, with a silky depth of musk, wild cherry, and forest floor that rewards patience and demands attention.

name: Domaine Gros Frère et Soeur Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru
desc_en_short: Domaine Gros Frère et Soeur's Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru is a benchmark expression of Burgundy's most storied walled vineyard — a majestic Pinot Noir offering silky tannins, ethereal red fruit, and earthy complexity from one of the Côte de Nuits' most revered family estates.

name: Domaine Gros Frère et Soeur Richebourg Grand Cru
desc_en_short: From one of Vosne-Romanée's most respected estates, this Richebourg Grand Cru from Domaine Gros Frère et Soeur delivers the breathtaking complexity and silken depth that Burgundy's most coveted 8-hectare grand cru vineyard is celebrated for — a truly exceptional Pinot Noir experience.

name: Domaine Georges Noellat Vosne-Romanee 1er Cru "Les Chaumes"
desc_en_short:
Georges Noellat was the nephew of Charles Noellat, who was once the proprietor of one of Vosne’s greatest domaines, a domaine who made important contributions to Domaines Jean-Jacques Confuron and Hudelot Noellat and even formed the vast majority of Domaine Leroy. As of 1990, Domaine Georges Noellat sold its production to Jadot and Drouhin for 20 years. Enter 20-year-old Maxime Cheurlin in 2010, who consequently took over the management of the estate from his grandmother.

Cheurlin grew up in Champagne, but it seems Burgundy wine is truly in his blood, as he is a nephew of the Jayer family and a cousin of Emmanuel Rouget’s sons. He complemented his winemaking studies at the Lycee du Viticole in Beaune with stages at Domaine Emmanuel Rouget and Domaine Gros Frere et Soeur in 2009.

name: Domaine Georges Noellat Nuits-Saint-Georges 1er Cru "Aux Boudots"
desc_en_short:
Georges Noellat was the nephew of Charles Noellat, who was once the proprietor of one of Vosne’s greatest domaines, a domaine who made important contributions to Domaines Jean-Jacques Confuron and Hudelot Noellat and even formed the vast majority of Domaine Leroy. As of 1990, Domaine Georges Noellat sold its production to Jadot and Drouhin for 20 years. Enter 20-year-old Maxime Cheurlin in 2010, who consequently took over the management of the estate from his grandmother.

Cheurlin grew up in Champagne, but it seems Burgundy wine is truly in his blood, as he is a nephew of the Jayer family and a cousin of Emmanuel Rouget’s sons. He complemented his winemaking studies at the Lycee du Viticole in Beaune with stages at Domaine Emmanuel Rouget and Domaine Gros Frere et Soeur in 2009.

name: Domaine Audiffred Vosne-Romanee 1er Cru "les Reignots"
desc_en_short:
The Audiffred field exploited since 1965 per Bernard and Henriette AUDIFFRED extends on 5 hectares, from Gevrey-Chambertin to Pommard. The family farm is a true passion, managed since the retirement of Bernard Henri AUDIFFRED by his son, who took over from his parents in 2007. The wines are manually bottled, not filtered or thickened. The method is traditional & natural, without changes of grounds, nor weeding. Only a regular tilling is practiced. The sulphating of the vines is containing copper and from suffers, without insecticides.

The wine makings are done by cold start (without yeast) which implies long cuvasions from 15 to 18 days, in wood tanks. The watering, the reassembly and the pigeage are made 3 times per day. The breeding is during 16 to 18 months out of barrels of oak. During this period, 2 rackings are made. Some vintages are bottled manually, the big volumes are put with a group of bottle-filling. The wines are bottled manually and underwent neither joining, nor filtering. White Beaune as for him has sudden the same manipulations as the red wines without before the bottling, a light filtration is practised, what implies that a light deposit can appear.

name: Domaine Jean-Pierre Guyon Vosne Romanee
desc_en_short:
Domaine Jean-Pierre Guyon moved towards organic viticulture during the 2000s. To bring clarity to our techniques of viticulture and vinification, we engaged in the process of ECOCERT accreditation in 2009, becoming certified in 2012.

As the harvest approaches, we taste the grapes in our different plots regularly, to decide on picking dates. This permits us to judge their ripeness. When the moment comes, the pickers advance, secateurs in hand, to pick the fruit which has been nurtured and cherished throughout the year.

name: Domaine Trapet Gevrey-Chambertin "Ostrea" (Magnum) (1.5 L)
desc_en_short: A biodynamically farmed village Gevrey-Chambertin from one of the appellation's most respected traditional estates, the 'Ostrea' magnum delivers Pinot Noir of striking purity and depth — shaped by century-old vines and Jean-Louis Trapet's uncompromising commitment to living soils.

name: Domaine Trapet Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Cru "Capita"
desc_en_short: With vines planted as far back as 1913, Domaine Trapet has firmly established itself as one of the great traditional estates in the Burgundian village of Gevrey-Chambertin. Jean-Louis met and married Andree, a wine grower from Alsace, and together they own top vineyards in both Alsace and Burgundy. Their quality is consistent with wine critics and lovers praising this husband and wife team as a force to be reckoned with. Jean-Louis Trapet has taken a departure from antiquated agricultural practices and is recognised as one of the producers at the forefront of the biodynamic movement. Ploughing is used instead of herbicides, and Trapet has placed a strict ban on the use of any chemical insecticides. The wines are made in Beaune.

desc_en_short: These five vine plots are situated on the northern slope of Gevrey-Chambertin called the “Côteau de Brochon”. Thanks to the small, concentrated berries produced by these plots of old vines, we find here all the richness and fruitiness of a Gevrey-Chambertin, its velvety smooth tannins, its superb freshness and its length on the palate.

desc_en_short: Very complex, long and deep, it needs time to open up. But when it is ready, it possesses every quality: a tightly-knit, velvety smooth texture, ripe, elegant fruitiness and an almost never-ending finish.

name: Domaine Denis Mortet Mazoyeres-Chambertin Grand Cru
desc_en_short: Denis Mortet, a key figure in Burgundy, began his career with his father at Domaine Charles Mortet and took over winemaking in the mid-1980s. Influenced by Henri Jayer and Lalou Bize Leroy, Denis founded his own domaine in 1992 with 4.5 hectares in Gevrey-Chambertin. Known for impeccable farming and richly textured wines, he expanded to 11 hectares, gaining a reputation for quality. After his sudden death in 2006, his son Arnaud, supported by his sister Clémence and mother Laurence, took over. Arnaud has refined the winemaking approach, focusing on elegance and precision while maintaining the domaine's esteemed legacy.

name: Domaine Hubert Lignier Clos de la Roche Grand Cru
desc_en_short:
Hubert and Laurent Lignier, father & son manages 9 hectares and make 24 wines (Bourgogne, Village, Premier and Grand Cru appellations). The vineyards are ploughed sinced 1990s, excluding weedkiller and insecticides. The 'climat' and great terroirs’ soils are firmly respected in order to favour micro-organism and therefore the essential balance for the vine’s growth.

Since 2011, the organic protective treatments were used for vinifications and ageing, their methods are little interventionist. The fruit’s quality is essential to craft 24 great wines. Wines are fresh, fine and elegant, which are also full bodied with a long lasting, mouth-watering finish. Each terroirs express themselves through the wines. Although, ageing in barrels (20 to 30% new oak) are rather long (20 or 22 months), on lees and without racking after malolactic fermentation. The wines are bottled using gravity without fining, in order to keep the wine’s freshness and its ageing potential.

desc_en_short: The Charmes-Chambertin sounds right the wine is accessible and charming even in it’s youth. The tannins are light and delicate. The wine is supple and with a very nice evolution potential.

desc_en_short: This diversity of terroirs gives a rich and dense wine, much closer to the roundness and finesse of Vosne-Romanée than the powerful of the classic Clos-Vougeot from the north of the appellation.

name: Domaine Thibault Liger-Belair Charmes-Chambertin Grand Cru "Aux Charmes" (Magnum) (1.5 L)
desc_en_short: This plot of 0.3 hectares was planted in 1954 and is located on the upper part of the Charmes-Chambertin terroir known as “Aux Charmes”. Running alongside the Route des Grands Crus between Morey-Saint-Denis and Gevrey-Chambertin, this plot is opposite the border between Latricières Chambertin and Chambertin itself.

name: Domaine Thibault Liger-Belair Richebourg Grand Cru
desc_en_short:
This wine always offers great depth and astonishing length and complexity. It is both structured and sophisticated.

One is often seeking superlatives to describe it, but sometimes, should we not simply allow ourselves to be carried away by a wine?

name: Domaine Pierre Girardin Vosne-Romanee 1er Cru "Les Suchots"
desc_en_short: Pierre Girardin is the 13th generation of his family to make wine in Burgundy. This brilliant yet youthful winegrower grew up learning in the vines and cellar of his father, Vincent Girardin. Pierre’s viticulture is organic, moving toward full certification. He follows the lunar calendar for every action and uses next-level pure compost from the family farm.

name: Domaine Pierre Girardin Montrachet Grand Cru
desc_en_short: From the 13th-generation winemaker Pierre Girardin, this organically farmed Montrachet Grand Cru represents Burgundy's most prestigious white appellation — yet the SKU is categorised as red wine, which warrants verification before purchase.

name: Domaine Pierre Girardin Griotte-Chambertin Grand Cru
desc_en_short: From one of Burgundy's most exciting young producers, Pierre Girardin's Griotte-Chambertin Grand Cru delivers the haunting floral intensity and silky, precise fruit that defines this tiny, revered climat — a benchmark expression of organic farming at its most thoughtful.

name: Domaine Pierre Girardin Richebourg Grand Cru
desc_en_short: From the 13th-generation vigneron Pierre Girardin, this Richebourg Grand Cru from the hallowed soils of Vosne-Romanée represents Burgundy's pinnacle — organically farmed Pinot Noir of breathtaking complexity, vinified with meticulous care and a deep respect for terroir.

name: Domaine Vincent Dancer Pommard 1er Cru 'Les Pézerolles'
desc_en_short: Vincent Dancer is a well-respected winemaker in Burgundy, known for his meticulous approach and focus on organic and biodynamic viticulture. While his whites from Chassagne-Montrachet and Meursault are particularly famous, his red wines, especially the Pommard, are also highly sought after. Since 2019, his son Théo has taken a leading role in the winemaking, continuing the family's dedication to high-quality, terroir-driven wines. The domaine is known for crafting elegant, pure, and refined wines.

name: Coessens Largillier Coteaux Champenois Vendange Egrappee - Rouge
Coessens Largillier Coteaux Champenois Vendange Entiere - Rouge
desc_en_short: Beautiful opening on the nose with flavors of strawberry, small red fruits and a well-integrated oak that is found on the palate. Powerful, invigorating with a beautiful width that is reminiscent of Pinot Noir.

name: Poupille Atypique - Cotes de Castillon
desc_en_short: Winemaker in Saint-Emilion, Jean-Marie Carrille purchased Chateau Poupille in 1967 and gave the management to his son Philippe Carrille in 1989, the 5th generation of wine producers. Poupille is located East of Bordeaux, 6 miles away from Saint-Emillion in Sainte Colombe. The estate is composed of old vines aged 35 years old in average. The vines face south at the top of hills. In local dialect Poupille means << end of the hill >> "Le Petit PETRUS" The wines were produced from a careful selection of best grapes coming from the oldest vines. Its production with low yields contributes to the development of a more concentrated wine, more suitable for aging in oak barrels. This wine is produced without sulfur.

name: Le Puy Retour des iles
desc_en_short: The Amoreau family,15 generations of winemakers since 1610. Located at the top of the same clay and fossil-rich limestone plateau as Saint-Emilion, overlooking the districts of Pomerol and Saint-Emilion, le Puy dominates the Dordogne Valley. At an altitude of 107m, it is the second-highest geodesic point of the Gironde department. This position lent its name to the site as of Roman times; le Puy means a high place, a podium, or a mountain peak.

name: Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret Vosne-Romanee Premier Cru "En Orveaux"
desc_en_short:
For more than eight generations, the Mongeard family has been established in Vosne-Romanée since the year 1620, right in the midst of the Côte de Nuits, producing wine with an utmost respect for tradition.

The Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret, renamed since 1945, now operates a large vineyard in the purist of the burgundy tradition. My grandfather was Eugène Mongeard and my grandmother Edmée Mugneret.

The property accounts today for approximately 30 hectares, spread on 35 different appellations producing white Burgundy issued from the Chardonnay grape, but also essentially red wines issued from the Pinot Noir grape in the best climates of the Côte.

name: Domaine Georges Noellat Beaune 1er Cru "Clos de la Mignotte"
desc_en_short: From the brilliant young vigneron Maxime Cheurlin, whose Burgundian bloodlines trace back to Henri Jayer and Charles Noellat, this Beaune Premier Cru from the intimate 'Clos de la Mignotte' vineyard delivers elegant, terroir-driven Pinot Noir with the precision and pedigree that has collectors paying close attention.

name: Domaine Georges Noellat Vosne-Romanee
desc_en_short:
Georges Noellat was the nephew of Charles Noellat, who was once the proprietor of one of Vosne’s greatest domaines, a domaine who made important contributions to Domaines Jean-Jacques Confuron and Hudelot Noellat and even formed the vast majority of Domaine Leroy. As of 1990, Domaine Georges Noellat sold its production to Jadot and Drouhin for 20 years. Enter 20-year-old Maxime Cheurlin in 2010, who consequently took over the management of the estate from his grandmother.

Cheurlin grew up in Champagne, but it seems Burgundy wine is truly in his blood, as he is a nephew of the Jayer family and a cousin of Emmanuel Rouget’s sons. He complemented his winemaking studies at the Lycee du Viticole in Beaune with stages at Domaine Emmanuel Rouget and Domaine Gros Frere et Soeur in 2009.

name: Domaine Audiffred  Morey-Saint-Denis
desc_en_short:
The Audiffred field exploited since 1965 per Bernard and Henriette AUDIFFRED extends on 5 hectares, from Gevrey-Chambertin to Pommard. The family farm is a true passion, managed since the retirement of Bernard Henri AUDIFFRED by his son, who took over from his parents in 2007. The wines are manually bottled, not filtered or thickened. The method is traditional & natural, without changes of grounds, nor weeding. Only a regular tilling is practiced. The sulphating of the vines is containing copper and from suffers, without insecticides.

The wine makings are done by cold start (without yeast) which implies long cuvasions from 15 to 18 days, in wood tanks. The watering, the reassembly and the pigeage are made 3 times per day. The breeding is during 16 to 18 months out of barrels of oak. During this period, 2 rackings are made. Some vintages are bottled manually, the big volumes are put with a group of bottle-filling. The wines are bottled manually and underwent neither joining, nor filtering. White Beaune as for him has sudden the same manipulations as the red wines without before the bottling, a light filtration is practised, what implies that a light deposit can appear.

name: Domaine Jean-Pierre Guyon Bourgogne Pinot Noir
desc_en_short:
Domaine Jean-Pierre Guyon moved towards organic viticulture during the 2000s. To bring clarity to our techniques of viticulture and vinification, we engaged in the process of ECOCERT accreditation in 2009, becoming certified in 2012.

As the harvest approaches, we taste the grapes in our different plots regularly, to decide on picking dates. This permits us to judge their ripeness. When the moment comes, the pickers advance, secateurs in hand, to pick the fruit which has been nurtured and cherished throughout the year.

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay "la Montagne"
desc_en_short: Domaine Sylvain Pataille is a relatively new estate in Marsannay – the estate was established by Sylvain in the late 1990s and the first vintage was 1999. Sylvain Pataille is an exciting young grower in Marsannay. He trained as an oenologist in Bordeaux, and still consults to 15 or so domaines in Burgundy. He began in 2001 with 4 ha and now has 14 ha mainly en fermage, which are undergoing conversion to biodynamic cultivation. He makes white from aligote and a selection of chardonnay rose, whose skin turns pink when ripe, as well as rose and red. He aims for very low yields in the reds of 35 hl/ha.

name: Domaine Claude Dugat Gevrey Chambertin
desc_en_short: Domaine Claude Dugat was established in 1955 and is widely considered one of the top producers in Gevrey-Chambertin. Farming practices at the Domaine are strictly sustainable and done without the use of any fertilizers or herbicides. Since 2013 they have been farming with an emphasis on organic procedures as well as incorporating some biodynamic practices.

name: Domaine Jean-Luc & Eric Burguet Gevrey-Chambertin "Mes Favorites" Vieilles Vignes (Magnum) (1.5 L)
desc_en_short:
Most of the 8 hectare domaine consists of village Gevrey Chambertin. Les Justices En Billard and En Reniard are bottled on their own, alongside two blends, a Gevrey Chambertin Tradition and his excellent ‘Mes Favorites’, made from old vines and favoured sites. There is also a small cuvee of premier cru Les Champeaux, just 0.18 ha. These are supplemented by 3 negociant cuvees Chambolle Musigny Les Chardannes Vosne Romanee 1er cru les Rouges and grand cru Chambertin Clos de Beze, so that Alain can try making different appellations.

Jean-Luc and Eric Burguet continue to put their own personal touches on the wines at the domaine. Focusing on biodynamic farming, gentle winemaking, and lesser amount of new oaks are among the recent developments at this small cellar in the heart of Gevrey. They aim to continue their father’s legacy of wines that are clean with very little sulfur, expressing their terroirs, and above all elegant. The goal for upcoming years is to find vines in a few Cote de Nuits appellations that are 1er Cru and Grand Cru, to further expand their range and be able to make wines from more legendary terroirs.

desc_en_short: A village-level Gevrey-Chambertin from the biodynamically farmed Domaine Trapet, 'Ostrea' expresses the iron-rich, oyster-fossil soils of this legendary Côte de Nuits appellation through a focused, herb-tinged Pinot Noir of real precision and old-vine depth.

name: Domaine Hubert Lignier Gevrey-Chambertin "Regnard"
desc_en_short:
Hubert and Laurent Lignier, father & son manages 9 hectares and make 24 wines (Bourgogne, Village, Premier and Grand Cru appellations). The vineyards are ploughed sinced 1990s, excluding weedkiller and insecticides. The 'climat' and great terroirs’ soils are firmly respected in order to favour micro-organism and therefore the essential balance for the vine’s growth.

Since 2011, the organic protective treatments were used for vinifications and ageing, their methods are little interventionist. The fruit’s quality is essential to craft 24 great wines. Wines are fresh, fine and elegant, which are also full bodied with a long lasting, mouth-watering finish. Each terroirs express themselves through the wines. Although, ageing in barrels (20 to 30% new oak) are rather long (20 or 22 months), on lees and without racking after malolactic fermentation. The wines are bottled using gravity without fining, in order to keep the wine’s freshness and its ageing potential.

Although, ageing in barrels (20 to 30% new oak) are rather long (20 or 22 months), on lees and without racking after malolactic fermentation. The wines are bottled using gravity without fining, in order to keep the wine’s freshness and its ageing potential.

name: Domaine Arlaud Morey Saint Denis 1er Cru "Les Millandes"
desc_en_short: Domaine Arlaud was founded in 1942 through the marriage of Joseph Arlaud and Renée Amiot, with the latter’s dowry including prime vineyard parcels in Burgundy. Joseph expanded the estate with strategic acquisitions starting in 1949. In 1966, the family acquired a historic 14th-century building for aging their wines, which is featured on their labels. Hervé Arlaud, who took over in 1983, and his wife Brigitte, expanded the estate, which their children managed together from 2004 to 2012. In 2003, the family transitioned to a modern facility in Morey-Saint-Denis, though the historic cellar in Nuits-Saint-Georges remains for the wine library and special tastings. Cyprien Arlaud took full control in 2013, overseeing a 15-hectare estate with 19 vineyard sites, including prized plots in four Grand Crus: Clos de la Roche, Clos Saint Denis, Charmes Chambertin, and Bonnes Mares.

desc_en_short: Felettig wines are traditionally crafted, and very representative of a style of Chambolle. With wine lovers and countless critics singing his praise it comes as no surprise that Gilbert is universally seen as one of the rising stars in Burgundy

name: Domaine Thibault Liger-Belair Gevrey-Chambertin "En Creot"
desc_en_short: The chalky soil gives this wine a beautiful freshness. Its unique location brings a purity worthy of certain grand crus from this appellation.

name: Domaine Thibault Liger-Belair Corton Grand Cru "Les Renardes"
desc_en_short:
Always with a great freshness thanks to the big presence of limestone in the soils, it’s a powerful wine without great wealth. This wine has a great depth and it is necessary to tame it to sense it perfectly.
This appellation is well known as Renardes, because its wines are always very rich with animal, leather and black fruit notes.

name: Domaine Henri Boillot Pommard 1er cru Clos Blanc - Rouge
desc_en_short: Henri is the 5th generation of the Boillot family. His son Guillaume joined the domaine a few years ago. In 2005 Henri Boillot bought out the shares of his brother and sister, and put his own name to his father’s domaine. The Domaine is now located in Meursault, consisting of 15 hectares split between white and red. Henri Boillot uses “lutte raisonne” meaning without using chemicals on the soil. White grapes are whole-bunch pressed, vinified without any batonage. The elevage is in 350L barrels, balance between new barrels and one year old barrels (never more). After fermentation the wine goes into the barrel, either new or one year old barrel. No racking, fining or filtering. The wines are bottled after 18 months in barrel and are generally described as pure, rich, accurate, powerful and brilliant.

desc_en_short: From a 13th-generation Burgundy family, Pierre Girardin's Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru Les Monts Luisants is a beautifully crafted Pinot Noir shaped by organically farmed vines on the Côte de Nuits' most luminous limestone slopes — precise, expressive, and built for the cellar.

name: Domaine Pierre Girardin Pommard 1er Cru "les Grands Epenots"
desc_en_short: Pierre Girardin is the 13th generation of his family to make wine in Burgundy. This brilliant yet youthful winegrower grew up learning in the vines and cellar of his father, Vincent Girardin. Pierre’s viticulture is organic, moving toward full certification. He follows the lunar calendar for every action and uses next-level pure compost from the family farm.
